title: vLLM audio transcription upload -- T1499 file fully buffered in memory before size-limit check
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-55646 (GHSA-v82g-2437-67m2,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), affecting vLLM from 0.22.0 to 0.23.0.

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` call
`request.file.read()` to fully materialize an uploaded audio file INTO
MEMORY before the documented `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB` size
limit (default 25 MB) is checked -- the check happens later, in the
speech-to-text preprocessing step. An API caller who can reach these
routes can submit a multipart upload far larger than the configured
limit and cause vLLM to allocate memory proportional to the FULL
uploaded size before the request is ever rejected as too large --
memory pressure or process termination depending on the deployment's
resource limits, entirely from a request that is ultimately going to
be refused anyway.

Detection logic flags a multipart upload to either audio endpoint whose
`Content-Length` exceeds the configured `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB`
limit by a wide margin -- the size-limit check existing at all means a
request this oversized was never going to succeed, so its presence on
the wire is itself the signal, independent of whether the request
eventually completes or the process survives it.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (vllm-project,
via GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix commit and PR), fixed in 0.24.0
(checks size before buffering, not after).
